narrative:
The model estimates a 47% chance that you will leave your job. Because this probability is high enough to flag risk, the company has decided to deny your promotion.

The decision was driven mainly by three key aspects of your profile. First, your total years of experience across all jobs had the strongest influence and pulled the prediction toward staying. Having only 1–5 years of overall experience is common among employees the model expects to remain (half of those predicted to stay fall in this same bracket), yet in your case the model still saw enough risk elsewhere to outweigh this stabilizing factor.

Two other factors pushed the prediction in the opposite direction, toward leaving. The fact that you have received other job offers while working here was the second most important signal. Employees who get external opportunities are noticeably more likely to leave. In addition, finding it difficult to balance work and personal life added further weight toward leaving. Only 9% of employees the model expects to stay report a difficult work–life balance, so this stands out as an important concern in your profile.

Taken together, the combination of external opportunities and work–life strain created enough concern to tip the prediction above the threshold, even though your limited overall experience would normally suggest stability.

The organization should discuss with you how to reduce work–life pressure and explore ways to match or exceed the external offers you have received. Addressing these two areas would most effectively lower the risk of losing you. (248 words)
